title: Introduce lazy-kernel-loader and ABI stability harness to reduce startup jitter and dependency surface
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: GPU node startup and runtime probe paths are brittle across our heterogeneous fleet (mixed CUDA versions, driver combinations, and Cutlass/Triton plugin variants). This shows up as probe jitter, occasional cold-start stalls, and larger dependency surface that forces conservative CI gates. Goal: implement a lazy-kernel-loader plus an ABI stability harness that reduces probe-time work, defers non-critical kernel instantiation until first use, and validates ABI compatibility in a controlled, observable way. Scope: (1) introduce a lazy loader layer that loads optimized kernels on demand, with a light-weight probe path for capability checks; (2) add an ABI-stability harness that runs deterministic micro-benchmarks at warmup to surface incompatibilities early and attach signals to the Console; (3) shrink the default runtime dependency matrix by splitting heavy plugin bundles into optional feature flags and feature-gated packages; (4) add rollout and rollback tooling for kernel bundles and a canary verification job.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start probe latency reduced by >=50% for 95th percentile on standard fleet compared to baseline (baseline measured 320ms)
Failed ABI mismatches detected and surfaced to Console with clear remediation steps (bundle/version suggestions)
No regression in token-throughput on steady-state benchmarks (+/-5% tolerance)
CI gate time for GPU images reduced by at least 30% by splitting optional plugin bundles
comments: 2026-02-17 - Discovery: Spike showed current probe path exercises full Cutlass/Triton plugin initialization even for short requests. Measured median probe ~110ms, p95 ~320ms on mixed fleet (A100, H100, older T4 dev nodes).

2026-02-22 - Design decision: Use a two-stage loader: (a) capability probe (lightweight symbol/driver checks + minimal kernel sanity), (b) lazy instantiation that binds full kernels on first actual op. This reduces startup I/O and serialization overhead. Jonah and Aisha agreed this keeps compatibility checks but defers expensive work.

2026-02-26 - Spike results: Implemented prototype lazy loader in runtime sandbox. Observed p95 probe drop from 320ms -> 85ms for short-lived worker processes. Throughput for 2k token workload unchanged within noise (+1.8%). See prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1219

2026-03-02 - Review notes from Runtime team (Ruchi): make lazy loader resilient to partial failures (e.g., missing opt kernels should fall back to reference kernels) and ensure KV cache priming not blocked by deferred kernel load. Added follow-up task to add a background prefetch heuristic for hot models.

2026-03-05 - Security review: no plaintext secrets in new loader. ABI harness will only run deterministic micro-benchmarks and not accept external input. Security signoff requested for KMS interactions but currently none required.

2026-03-07 - QA: Integration test added in CI to validate lazy-load fallback on nodes with artificially removed plugin artifacts. New test job: runtime-lazy-load-canary (runs on a small set of fleet images).

2026-03-09 - Ops feedback: Add metrics to Console for: (1) lazy-load latency histogram, (2) number of fallback kernel loads, (3) ABI-harness failures per image. Also recommend linking to rollout dashboard for canary rollout.
2026-03-10 - Current blockers: need infra permission to deploy canary images in ap-southeast-1. Eng infra ticket opened (ENG-143601). Preparing deployment plan and rollback runbook.
implementation_notes: Split bundles: create runtime-core + runtime-optional-kernels packages. Optional kernels installed via a feature flag (RUNTIME_OPTIONAL_KERNELS). Default image uses core only to reduce CI surface.

Loader API: expose async load_kernel(kernel_id) that returns immediately with a Future; first call to execute op awaits completion. Add a non-blocking fast_path that uses reference kernels when optional fails.

ABI harness: small deterministic conv/gemm kernel runner (single-threaded, fixed seed) that compares known-good outputs for a given kernel-version pair. Results written to /var/log/runtime/abi-harness.<sha>.log and surfaced via Console ingest.
Benchmarks: use the existing perf harness and test traces. Baseline runs are stored in GCS: gs://redwood-ci/runtime/perf-baselines/2026-02-10/

CI changes: new docker build stage to produce core + optional artifacts and publish optional tarballs to internal mirror. Reduce full-image CI gate by skipping optional kernel validation on every commit; run nightly bundle validation instead.
qa_plan: Canary rollout to 5% of dedicated pool for 48 hours with synthetic traffic in staging (traffic replay). Monitor lazy-load latency, fallback rate, and token throughput.
Run ABI-harness nightly across all image tags for a week and compare results to baseline. Fail build if harness produces mismatches across majority of nodes.
Test failure scenarios: simulate missing plugin files, driver mismatch, and low-memory OOM during lazy-load to validate recovery and logging.
Add e2e smoke test in console that triggers a small model run and validates response correctness when optional-kernels are not present.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy core-only images to staging and run perf + canary jobs (2026-03-16)
Phase 2: Canary deploy lazy-loader and ABI harness to 5% of production nodes in us-west-2 for 48h (2026-03-18)
Phase 3: Expand to 25% with additional monitoring and run cost/latency regression checks (2026-03-21)
Phase 4: Full fleet rollout if no regressions after 7 days (target 2026-03-28)
followups: Add background prefetch heuristic for hot models (ENG-143752)
Integrate ABI harness results into Console regression alerts (ENG-144001)
Document recommended dependency matrix and deprecation schedule for legacy plugin bundles (PM to review)
